correctness.rationale: The stationary output is a shift-equivariant factor of stationary base times independent Bernoulli and uniform processes; ergodicity passes by weak mixing of Bernoulli shifts. Conditioning on the whole input makes each coordinate-window event independent, with probability at most q=1-epsilon(1-2r). Thus sharp q^(2N+1) holds for every N and all dependent stationary laws; the all-half deterministic process saturates each finite bound. The metric includes the zeroth coordinate with coefficient one, giving null infinite dynamical balls. A stationary joining has cost <=epsilon/2 and a deterministic zero input forces equality among all joinings. Coarse M-bin entropy conditional on input equals H_epsilon(M) per coordinate, hence infinite KS entropy. Domain endpoints and limiting quantifiers were checked, and 1848 finite exact-rational tests plus 15 numerical entropy diagnostics passed (not used as infinite proof).

value.rationale: Invariant and ergodic constraints are absent from the motivating density theorem and cannot be obtained by its conditional reweighting. A sharp universal bar-d perturbation bound, sharp uniform anti-concentration for arbitrarily dependent input, and exact infinite-entropy cost give an actionable structural approximation theorem rather than mere known product special cases. It extends a recent natural Hilbert-cube shift question to robust stationary laws while articulating the entropy tradeoff.
